sentences.cn_text: 彼得斯喜欢在风景中拍摄蝴蝶，既颂扬昆虫本身，也礼赞其周围环境之美。
sentences.en_text: Peters likes to photograph butterflies in a landscape, celebrating the beauty of their surroundings as well as the insects themselves.

sentences.cn_text: 他拍摄的格兰维尔豹蛱蝶从怀特岛康普顿湾白垩悬崖旁的海石竹中振翅而起的照片尤为壮美。
sentences.en_text: His pictures of a Glanville fritillary rising from the sea-pinks beside the chalk cliffs of Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight are particularly glorious.

sentences.cn_text: 这些起飞镜头更具挑战性，因为需要使用广角镜头，这意味着他与蝴蝶的距离必须不到2厘米。
sentences.en_text: These take-off shots are even more challenging because they require a wide-angle lens, which means he must be less than 2cm from the butterfly.

sentences.cn_text: 要如此接近一只受阳光温暖而变得敏感易惊的昆虫，难度极大。
sentences.en_text: It’s incredibly difficult to get that close to a skittish sun-warmed insect.

sentences.cn_text: 不同于某些摄影师将昆虫置于冰箱中减缓其活动的「作弊」做法，彼得斯拒绝干扰野生蝴蝶。
sentences.en_text: Unlike some photographers, who “cheat” by keeping insects in a fridge to slow them down, Peters refuses to tamper with wild butterflies.

sentences.cn_text: 彼得斯的标志性作品是蝴蝶「起飞」照片，在单帧画面中展现一只蝴蝶从花朵上起飞时的多次振翅动作。
sentences.en_text: Peters’ signature shot is a butterfly “take-off”, showing the multiple wing-beats of one butterfly in one frame as it lifts off from a flower.

sentences.cn_text: 他是如何捕捉到这一画面的？
sentences.en_text: How does he capture it?

sentences.cn_text: 技术提供了帮助。
sentences.en_text: Technology helps.

sentences.cn_text: 一台典型的数码单反相机每秒拍摄20帧。
sentences.en_text: A typical digital SLR camera shoots 20 frames a second.

sentences.cn_text: 他使用的高速OM系统相机每秒可拍摄120帧。
sentences.en_text: He uses a high-speed OM System which shoots 120 frames a second.

sentences.cn_text: 与欧洲大陆相比，英国的蝴蝶物种相对较少，其中80%的物种数量正在减少，主要原因是集约化化学农业将许多物种的栖息地缩减为零散碎片和小型自然保护区。
sentences.en_text: Britain has relatively few butterfly species compared with mainland Europe and 80% are in decline, mostly because intensive chemical farming has reduced many species to tiny fragments of habitat and small nature reserves.

sentences.cn_text: 全球变暖使某些物种受益，但其他物种因过于孤立而无法找到合适的新栖息地，而园艺习惯——如用硬质铺装覆盖花园和使用杀虫剂——同样无益。
sentences.en_text: Global heating is benefiting some species but others are too isolated to find suitable new habitat, and gardening habits — paving over gardens and using pesticides — aren’t helping either.

sentences.cn_text: 蝴蝶的授粉能力或许不及野生蜜蜂和食蚜蝇，但由于英国蝴蝶是世界上研究最为充分的昆虫类群，它们成为飞行昆虫广泛衰退的极有价值的指示物种。
sentences.en_text: Butterflies may not pollinate as many plants as wild bees and hoverflies, but because British butterflies are the best-studied group of insects in the world, they are an extremely useful indicator of the wider declines in flying insects.

sentences.cn_text: 五年前夏末，安德鲁·福塞克·彼得斯被诊断患有肠癌。
sentences.en_text: Five years ago, at summer’s end, Andrew Fusek Peters was diagnosed with bowel cancer.

sentences.cn_text: 「我在等待手术，感觉非常不适，坐在自家花园里。
sentences.en_text: “I was waiting for surgery, feeling really ill, sitting in my garden.

sentences.cn_text: 天气极好，到处都是赤蛱蝶，」他说。
sentences.en_text: It was amazing weather and there were painted lady butterflies everywhere,” he says.

sentences.cn_text: 「它们是脆弱生命的象征，是希望与抗争的象征，某种东西触动了我的灵魂。」
sentences.en_text: “They were a symbol of fragile life, of hope and defiance, and something appealed to my soul.”

sentences.cn_text: 这使得拍摄听起来既简单又做作，但彼得斯坚称这仍是一项巨大的挑战。
sentences.en_text: That makes it sound easy, and artificial, but Peters insists it is still a massive challenge.

sentences.cn_text: 他通常需要拍摄一万到两万张照片，才能获得一组对焦清晰的蝴蝶起飞序列。
sentences.en_text: He typically takes between 10,000 and 20,000 shots to get one butterfly take-off sequence in focus.

sentences.cn_text: 在如此高的快门速度下，景深极浅，而蝴蝶不会沿直线飞行，它们会迅速飞出焦点范围。
sentences.en_text: At such high shutter speeds, the depth of field is tiny, and as butterflies do not fly in a straight line they swiftly flutter out of focus.

sentences.cn_text: 除了数千次尝试，还需要耐心与野外技巧来预判蝴蝶可能的飞行路线，并在对焦状态下将其捕捉。
sentences.en_text: As well as thousands of attempts, it takes patience and fieldcraft to anticipate a butterfly’s likely flight-line — and catch it — in focus.

sentences.cn_text: 那么，为追逐一种难以捉摸、快速移动的野生动物而度过漫长而汗流浃背的一天，吸引力何在？
sentences.en_text: So what’s the appeal of a long, sweaty day in pursuit of an elusive, fast-moving wild animal?

sentences.cn_text: 「这感觉真是棒极了，」彼得斯说。
sentences.en_text: “It just feels bloody brilliant,” says Peters.

sentences.cn_text: 「如果我度过了充实的一天，与蝴蝶有过美好的邂逅，结识了有趣的蝴蝶爱好者，并拍到了一些精彩的照片，那就成为我精神银行中的一笔财富。
sentences.en_text: “If I’ve had a full day of good encounters with butterflies, met interesting butterfly people and I’ve got some good shots, that becomes a vault in my spiritual bank.

sentences.cn_text: 这是一种幸福的感觉。」
sentences.en_text: It’s a happy feeling.”

sentences.cn_text: 作为一名儿童作家和诗人，同时也是一位热衷的业余摄影师，彼得斯观察着蝴蝶，并随意地想知道自己能否捕捉到它们飞行的瞬间。
sentences.en_text: A children’s author and poet who had become a keen amateur photographer, Peters watched the butterflies and idly wondered if he could capture them in flight.

sentences.cn_text: 在成功接受癌症切除手术并康复期间，这迅速成为他的一种痴迷。
sentences.en_text: It swiftly became an obsession as he recovered from a successful operation to remove the cancer.

sentences.cn_text: 近几个夏天，他走遍英国各地，拍摄了全部58种本土蝴蝶物种。
sentences.en_text: In recent summers, he has travelled the length and breadth of Britain to photograph all 58 native species of butterfly.

sentences.cn_text: 如今，那些夏日的成果已结集成一本精美的新书出版。
sentences.en_text: Now the fruits of those summers have been published in a beautiful new book.

sentences.cn_text: 蝴蝶起飞速度极快，人仍然无法反应得足够快来捕捉起飞瞬间，但若他半按快门，相机会保存他实际按下快门前的70帧画面。
sentences.en_text: A butterfly takes off so quickly it is still impossible to react quickly enough to capture that take-off but if he half-presses the shutter, the camera saves the 70 previous frames before the moment he actually takes the picture.

sentences.cn_text: 「这就像时间旅行，所以我不会错过起飞的瞬间，」他说。
sentences.en_text: “It’s time travel, so I don’t miss the moment of take-off,” he says.

sentences.cn_text: 捕捉到蝴蝶起飞画面后，他会在Photoshop中将10到15帧画面叠加合成。
sentences.en_text: After he’s captured the butterfly taking off, he layers 10 to 15 frames together in Photoshop.
